final_candidates.decision_summary: Conservative lysine-to-arginine substitution in the stalk could preserve the basic character while altering electrostatic contacts involved in G-F triggering. WT K75 is consistent with the provided sequence.
Neutralization of a membrane-proximal acidic side chain may improve conformational transmission to F if local negative charge suppresses fusion activation. WT E70 is confirmed in the sequence.

stop_reason.detail: Further LLM-only iteration is unlikely to provide better discrimination among the current conservative candidates.

history.rationale: Conservative lysine-to-arginine change in the stalk region may modulate electrostatic contacts involved in G-F triggering without drastic chemistry. WT K75 is confirmed from the N-terminal stalk segment.

Charge-neutralizing but size-conservative substitution near the TM/stalk boundary could improve fusion activation if local negative charge is unfavorable. Position 70 is verified as E in the sequence.
Histidine removal in the stalk could reduce inhibitory polar contacts and change triggering dynamics, but loss of H bonding is a risk. WT H86 is verified.

Acid-to-amide change at the stalk/head transition may enhance receptor-induced conformational coupling if local negative charge limits entry. Position 149 is verified as D, but head-proximal effects are uncertain.
Conservative basic-residue swap in the head-proximal region is likely tolerated and may fine-tune interactions; however effect size is expected to be small. WT R172 is verified.
